oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and documents them as interchangeable.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical access_token and id_token claim sets as token confusion by itself; this is documented platform behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: The /api/userinfo response only includes claims allowed by the granted scope.
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of profile or email fields is expected when those scopes were not requested.

oidc_jwt.description: Bearer access tokens are standard OAuth tokens without documented jti replay prevention; reuse of the same token is expected for stateless verification.
oidc_jwt.note: Replay of the same JWT bearer token should not be reported as an anti-replay failure unless testing a context that explicitly requires one-time use.

oidc_jwt.description: On SSO logout, Casdoor invalidates tokens by setting ExpiresIn to 0 or a negative value; introspection and refresh then reject them.
oidc_jwt.note: Post-logout token rejection may be implemented through server-side expiry metadata rather than JWT cryptographic revocation.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor can automatically link OAuth logins to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone, or username case-insensitively.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity merges caused by documented account-linking rules are not necessarily principal-binding vulnerabilities.

oidc_jwt.description: Using authorization_code grant with code=guest-user creates a guest account named guest_<uuid> with tag guest-user.
oidc_jwt.note: A granted identity prefixed with guest_ in this flow is expected and not an identity confusion bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Shared applications intentionally use organization-specific client_id/application-name suffixes of the form -org-<organizationName>.
oidc_jwt.note: Different effective client identifiers across organizations are expected for shared applications.

oidc_jwt.description: When SAML username mapping is absent or empty, Casdoor falls back to email, then NameID, for username creation.
oidc_jwt.note: This is documented fallback behavior for SAML providers and not an arbitrary identity mix-up.

oidc_jwt.description: Session-based authentication to the MCP server bypasses scope checking and grants full tool access.
oidc_jwt.note: Use bearer tokens for scope enforcement tests; cookie-auth full access is documented behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and allows them to be used interchangeably.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical access_token and id_token contents as token confusion by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: SSO logout without logoutAll=false logs the user out from all sessions and expires all tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-session invalidation after default logout is expected behavior, not session confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Applications with exclusive sign-in enabled intentionally terminate previous sessions for the same user and application on new login.
oidc_jwt.note: Loss of older sessions after a new login is by design.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch and normal authorization-code tests, the redirect_uri used in start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token MUST match exactly, character-for-character, including scheme, host, port, path, and trailing slash. Casdoor documentation states redirect URI mismatches fail the flow.

For I5 audience-binding tests, use the OAuth resource indicator parameter `resource` in BOTH start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token. Casdoor requires the resource to match exactly between authorization and token requests; otherwise failures are setup errors, not audience-enforcement findings.

For I3 PKCE tests, when PKCE is enabled the token request MUST include `code_verifier`. Casdoor documents that `client_secret` becomes optional under PKCE, but if provided it must be correct. Do not interpret failures from missing/incorrect code_verifier as unrelated security behavior.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL login using a valid token acquisition path in the same application configuration. Without a successful control flow, a failed attack flow may reflect broken client/app setup rather than token-time enforcement.

Casdoor access tokens are JWTs and are stateless bearer tokens. Do NOT treat replay of the same bearer token as an I2 vulnerability by itself. The documentation describes standard OAuth token issuance and introspection but no jti replay tracking; replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti are by-design for this platform unless a special one-time context is documented.

Refresh token expiration has a numeric sentinel: application `Refresh Token` expiration default is `0` hours. In Casdoor, `0` does NOT mean immediate expiry; it is the documented default configuration value. Do not assume zero disables refresh or means expired-at-once without confirming application behavior.

Application `Code resend timeout` has a numeric sentinel: value `0` means use the global default, not literal zero-second resend. Never assume `0` disables throttling; it selects the platform default countdown.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, request a narrower original scope first, then exchange with an expanded scope. Casdoor documents that omitted scope inherits the subject token scope, and specified scope is intended for narrowing. Any broader exchanged scope than originally authorized is the relevant signal.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, map the abstract audience parameter to Casdoor's `resource` field on /api/login/oauth/access_token. Casdoor uses RFC 8707 resource indicators to set the access token `aud` claim; testing audience binding without setting `resource` will not exercise the intended control.

For I4 multi-organization tests on shared applications, Casdoor shared applications require app references using the suffix `-org-<organizationName>` in the client_id or application name. Reusing the unsuffixed client_id across orgs tests the wrong principal namespace and can create false collision results.

Casdoor can automatically link OAuth logins to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. For I4 collision tests involving federated identities, account linking by email/username is a documented platform behavior and must be controlled or disabled in test design to avoid false positives.

For I4 case-confusion tests, Casdoor documentation explicitly states automatic account linking may use username case-insensitively. Treat case-only merges as potentially by-design unless the test isolates a context where distinct principals should remain separate.

For I4 username normalization tests, organization setting `isUsernameLowered` can convert usernames to lowercase. If enabled in the target deployment, case-variant identities will collapse by configuration; do not report this as an unexpected collision without first accounting for that setting.

For I4 provider-specific identity mapping tests, some OAuth providers intentionally choose non-email stable identifiers as usernames: Lark uses UserId then UnionId then OpenId; DingTalk uses unionid; Baidu may use a masked username. Compare against the provider-mapped identity semantics, not the human-readable email, when evaluating principal binding.

For I5 scope-based authorization tests against MCP or other scoped APIs, session/cookie authentication bypasses scope checking and grants full access by design. Use Bearer access tokens, not browser sessions, when testing whether granted permissions exceed requested scopes.

For I5 custom-scope tests, custom scopes are available only for applications with category `Agent`. Default applications expose only standard OIDC scopes. Do not request custom scopes on non-Agent apps and interpret rejection as a vulnerability.

For I3 config-change sequences involving application settings such as default grant types, PKCE, token format, or redirect URIs, a valid test must show that NEW logins reflect the updated configuration. Casdoor documentation describes immediate use of current application settings; do not treat behavior changes after admin reconfiguration as stale-session bugs unless the same request is evaluated inconsistently.

Casdoor's token endpoint /api/login/oauth/access_token is documented with JSON request bodies for authorization_code, password, client_credentials, and token-exchange flows. The fuzzer MUST send JSON for these flows, even though introspection uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

For authorization code flows using RFC 8707 resource indicators, the resource parameter MUST match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. If they differ, audience-binding tests will fail for setup reasons rather than security reasons.

Application Redirect URLs must exactly match the redirect_uri used in authorization requests, including scheme, host, port, path, and trailing slash. Casdoor documentation repeatedly distinguishes provider callback URL (Casdoor /callback) from application Redirect URL (client callback).

Refresh token lifetime has a numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. In Casdoor, 0 is a special default value, not a literal positive lifetime to rely on. The fuzzer MUST explicitly configure a nonzero refresh lifetime when refresh-dependent sequences are needed and MUST NOT assume 0 means a usable long-lived refresh token.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control login with a valid token/code flow in the same application configuration. Without a control, token rejection cannot be distinguished from misconfigured client_id, redirect_uri, or disabled grant type.

For I3 PKCE-related sequences, Casdoor supports PKCE but it is optional unless the client/application enables it. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat successful code exchange without code_verifier as a vulnerability unless PKCE was explicitly enabled for that application or provider flow.

For I3 config-change tests involving grant types, Casdoor requires non-default grant types to be enabled on the application edit page. A failed password or token-exchange request may reflect disabled grant type rather than security enforcement. The fuzzer MUST ensure the target grant type is enabled before testing.

For I5 audience-binding tests, Casdoor sets the access token aud claim to the resource URI when the resource parameter is supplied; otherwise audience behavior follows the client/application default (often client ID). The fuzzer MUST explicitly set resource when testing audience isolation and MUST verify aud via introspection or token parsing.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, Casdoor documentation states that omitted scope inherits the subject token scope, while provided scope is intended for narrowing. The fuzzer MUST compare exchanged-token scope and claims against the original token and requested scope; requesting broader scope than the subject token is the attack case.
Casdoor access_token and id_token are by design the same JWT payload. The fuzzer MUST treat equality of access_token and id_token claims as normal behavior, not token confusion or over-issuance.

Casdoor userinfo returns claims according to requested scope. Missing profile/email/address/phone fields in /api/userinfo are not authorization failures if those scopes were not requested. The fuzzer MUST request the needed scopes before asserting missing claims as bugs.

For logout and freshness tests, Casdoor invalidates tokens on SSO logout by setting ExpiresIn to 0 or a negative value, and introspection/refresh reject tokens with ExpiresIn <= 0. The fuzzer SHOULD verify post-logout invalidation via introspection or protected API access rather than assuming JWT cryptographic validity alone implies session validity.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch and PKCE-related OIDC tests, start_oidc_auth MUST use /login/oauth/authorize and exchange_code_for_token MUST use /api/login/oauth/access_token. The token request body is documented as JSON here, and the redirect_uri/resource values must match the authorization request exactly when used. A mismatch is expected to fail by design and should be asserted via non-2xx status, not identity comparison.

Casdoor supports PKCE on the authorization code flow. When code_challenge/code_challenge_method=S256 are sent at start_oidc_auth, exchange_code_for_token SHOULD include code_verifier. With PKCE enabled, client_secret becomes optional, but if provided it must be correct. For pkce_skip-style tests, assert token exchange failure by HTTP status rather than treating it as an identity bug.

For I5 audience-binding tests using RFC 8707 resource indicators, if start_oidc_auth includes resource, exchange_code_for_token MUST include the same resource value exactly. Casdoor documents that the resource must match exactly between authorization and token requests; otherwise failure is by design and not an authorization-binding vulnerability.

For I2 freshness tests on authorization-code tokens, include a CONTROL login using a valid code/token flow alongside the ATTACK case. Without a control, a failed exchange or userinfo call cannot be distinguished from broken application configuration, redirect URI mismatch, missing grant enablement, or PKCE/resource mismatch.

Refresh token expiration has a numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. In Casdoor, 0 means the platform default configuration value, not necessarily immediate expiry. Do not assume 0 disables refresh or means zero lifetime; explicitly configure a positive value when tests require refresh behavior.

Code resend timeout has a numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout set to 0 means use the global default, not literal zero seconds. Do not interpret 0 as 'no wait' in tests that depend on verification-code timing.

Cookie/session lifetime has a numeric sentinel: CookieExpireInHours of 0 means use the default session cookie lifetime, not immediate expiry. Documentation also states that without 'Remember me', session is limited to 24 hours. Do not use 0 when a precise session lifetime is required for testing.

Casdoor documents that access_token and id_token are the same JWT payload and can be used interchangeably for authentication/authorization. This is by design. The fuzzer MUST still treat access_token as session_token for API calls, but should not flag identical access_token/id_token contents as a token confusion bug.

Casdoor token invalidation on SSO logout is stateful: logout sets ExpiresIn to 0 or a negative value, and introspection/refresh reject tokens with ExpiresIn <= 0. For I2 logout/revocation tests, verify revocation via introspect_token active=false or failed protected-resource access after /api/sso-logout, not by assuming JWT signature expiry alone.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, Casdoor documents that requested scope should be a subset of the original token scope, and omitting scope inherits the subject token scope. The fuzzer MUST compare exchanged-token scope/claims against the original authorization and treat inherited same-scope behavior as expected, not as escalation.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti on oidc_jwt, do NOT flag reuse of the same access token as a vulnerability by itself. Casdoor documents standard OAuth/JWT bearer usage and does not document jti replay tracking for access tokens; bearer-token replay is expected for stateless JWT validation unless a stateful revocation event occurs.

For I4 multi-organization/shared-application tests, shared applications require the client_id or application name to be suffixed with -org-<organizationName>. If this suffix is omitted, authentication may target the wrong organization by design. Use organization-qualified client identifiers when testing cross-org identity separation.

Casdoor can automatically link OAuth logins to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone (if enabled), or username (case-insensitive). For I4 collision tests, account linking can intentionally merge identities. The fuzzer MUST distinguish configured linking behavior from unintended principal collapse and avoid flagging documented case-insensitive username linking as a bug.

When testing I4 case_confusion, note that Casdoor documentation states automatic account linking may occur by username case-insensitively. 'Admin' and 'admin' may intentionally resolve to the same account under linking rules; this is a by-design behavior unless the test disables or avoids linking paths.

For OIDC userinfo verification, returned claims depend on requested scope. If verify_granted_identity is expected to include email/profile/address/phone claims, the original authorization/token request MUST include the corresponding scopes. Missing claims without requested scope are by design and not evidence of authorization stripping or identity confusion.

I5 MUST include a cross-tenant token exchange test: create org-A with app-A and user-A, create org-B with app-B. Login user-A via password grant to app-A to get subject_token. Then call token_exchange with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange, client_id=app-B-clientId, client_secret=app-B-clientSecret, subject_token=user-A-access-token, subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token. If exchange succeeds, the subject_token from org-A was accepted by org-B app — cross-org escalation. Casdoor uses shared cert-built-in across all apps, so JWT signatures validate cross-org.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Applications and providers use owner='admin'. Users use owner=organization_name (e.g., 'test-org'). Always include 'owner' in create/update API calls.
